scope: Selected steel simple helmet and plate armor, actual crafting and movement; Sharp/Blunt coverage, penetration, durability and damage-worker integration. Controlled tests, ordinary campaign, historical saves and native experiments are separate evidence.

armorTests.title: migrates genuine v16 apparel bytes without replacing clothes, wounds or resources
migrates genuine v16 trauma bytes without replacing clothes, wounds or resources
rejects new armor fields and records smuggled into v16 rather than granting new technology or gear
rejects malformed recipes, incompatible jobs, changed costs and duplicated identities in v17
delivers steel, resumes unfinished work exactly and produces one unique helmet without duplicating a reservation
checks PlateArmor research and Crafting 7 before assigning production or reserving its steel
keeps in-flight cargo when paused and returns the same steel rather than consuming or duplicating it
persists cancelled delivered steel while the floor is full and refunds it exactly once after space opens
deflects real melee while reducing durability, and destroys a last-HP garment once without dropping a duplicate
retains a carried garment when a mid-wear loss leaves no remaining covered parts
slows real travel in plate and retains its remaining route through a save
matches separately extracted source declarations and complete Human coverage
separates tailor/smithy recipes and preserves original work, costs and requirements
uses armor-specific quality factors and never scales rating or max HP by current HP
checks material, six-field identity and positive surviving HP strictly
covers actual groups, including internal organs, without extending to hands, feet or face
uses all occupied layers for conflicts and sorts by the last native layer
applies equipped movement offset before Moving and the native minimum, relative to grid speed
uses strict threshold at armor roll 0.404999
uses strict threshold at armor roll 0.405
uses strict threshold at armor roll 0.809999
uses strict threshold at armor roll 0.81
subtracts penetration but still damages apparel and samples zero-rating layers
uses ordered apparel, one check for multilayer plate, and cached original Sharp stat after conversion
uses pre-impact rating when the garment is destroyed, then removes it from later hits
consumes random rounding for integral durability/half damage and reports zero rounded half damage
does not damage uncovered apparel and consumes only natural armor for a bare hit
validates all inputs and random values without mutating original garments
protects the actual forced internal Stab target and retains Stab propagation after conversion
retains original Stab outside-preservation thresholds after Sharp becomes Blunt
retains Cut cleave after conversion, without rerunning armor on propagated body parts
uses effective damage Def for Bite duplicate-to-outside instead of switching workers
returns armor durability on a full block without creating wounds or allocating injury IDs
keeps trauma and clothing atomic on failed armor, propagation RNG or allocated IDs

campaign.scope: Fresh v17 colony. Only normal commands, step, save/load; terrain/path/state are read-only observations. No injected resources, research, skills, positions, health, armor or time. Real underground steel, upper-floor research and smithy, fuel, quality, equipment and scheduled raid. Single ordinary campaign is not a probability measurement.

mainPageIsolateHeapObservation.interpretation: Natural GC/JIT noise is retained. This is one page isolate and is not a whole-page or whole-browser leak/capacity claim.

failedAttempts.scope: Initial generated upper floor did not include the smithy front operating aisle; normal placement correctly rejected it. The scenario now builds that aisle with real floor jobs.

A whole-job deep equality assertion incorrectly expected ordinary runtime reservations/reason strings to survive loader reconciliation. It now checks IDs, materials, progress, work clocks and quality while allowing normal worker reassignment. No production rule was relaxed.

The conservation audit originally omitted external raider equipment. It now records actual arrival/exit item IDs separately from colony production; the production ledger and gameplay were not altered.

The first animation and item inspections projected below the HUD. The script now pans via ordinary WASD before asserting visible bounds. A duplicate apparel detail locator is scoped to the ground-item inspector; all original gameplay assertions remain.

limitations: 20 TPS, 12000-tick days and integer grid-step timing remain project adaptations. Plate uses the native 4.6-relative movement modifier, then rounds the existing 4/6-tick grid baseline; not exact native path timing.
Project keyed RNG is [0,1); native Rand can include 1. No Unity random-stream replay or float-bit equivalence.
Only Sharp and Blunt melee damage paths use protection. Heat armor is displayed data, not a fire or ranged combat system.

Controlled integration fixtures prove full deflection, one-HP destruction and awkward output space. A single normal raid has separately recorded equipment/injury outcomes and does not measure armor probabilities.
Native Dev damage setup is a separate experiment, not normal gameplay acquisition. Web browser checks use read-only state and projection, not screen-only perception.
Six lifecycle cycles observe renderer convergence and the main page heap only, excluding workers, native allocations and GPU memory; no whole-browser capacity or long-duration leak guarantee.
No shield, additional armor materials, full stun/instant-kill protection, infection/surgery/implants or social systems.
